question: How well do LLMs act as agents across diverse interactive environments, and why do they fail?
contributions: Introduce evaluating LLMs as agents and AgentBench: 8 environments in 3 grounding types
Evaluate 29 LLMs, finding a large gap between API-based and OSS models <=70B, and analyse failure reasons
Release an integrated server-client evaluation toolkit with datasets and environments

method.summary: Eight interactive environments (OS, DB, KG, DCG, LTP, HH, WS, WB) wrapped in a server-client toolkit; 29 LLMs prompted with CoT at temperature 0 and scored per task, then combined into a weighted overall score.

datasets.name: Operating System (OS)
datasets.source: about half human-written from 6000 Stack Overflow bash problems, half gpt-4 generated and unit-test filtered; 8 annotators, ~2h each

datasets.name: Database (DB)
datasets.source: WikiSQL, WikiTableQuestions, SQA, HybridaQA, FeTaQA; gpt-3.5-turbo augmented (10 new rows, 5 SQL each, rephrased)

datasets.name: Knowledge Graph (KG)
datasets.split: App D says first 500 tasks used for evaluation
datasets.source: GrailQA, ComplexWebQuestions, GraphQuestions on Freebase via Virtuoso; questions needing >=5 tool calls

datasets.name: Digital Card Game (DCG, Aquawar)
datasets.source: 2021 THU Agent Competition Aquawar; opponent is algorithmic (random / greedy baselines)
datasets.preprocessing: two stages (without / with assertions), averaged; 5 chances for legal format

datasets.name: Lateral Thinking Puzzles (LTP)
datasets.source: web puzzles, four difficulty levels; key points summarised by gpt-3.5-turbo
datasets.preprocessing: host is an LLM system (gpt-3.5-turbo); max round e.g. 25

datasets.name: House Holding (ALFWorld)
datasets.size: 50 test / 20 dev (Table 2); 134 solvable problems from eval out-of-distribution split (App G)
datasets.preprocessing: 1-shot per category, BLEU fallback for invalid output, 3 identical outputs = failure

datasets.name: Web Shopping (WebShop)
datasets.size: 200 test / 80 dev (Table 2); first 500 of 12,087 instructions (App H)

datasets.name: Web Browsing (Mind2Web)
datasets.size: 100 test / 31 dev (Table 2); Cross Domain set 912 tasks, 73 websites (App I)
datasets.preprocessing: DeBERTa-style ranker picks top-k; top-10 candidates, 5 shown per round, 3-example CoT

models.name: API: gpt-4 0613, gpt-3.5-turbo 0613, text-davinci-003, text-davinci-002 (2,048 context), claude-3 opus, claude-2, claude v1.3, claude-instant v1.1, chat-bison-001, glm-4

OSS: llama2-70b/13b/7b chat; guanaco-65b/33b; vicuna-33b v1.3, 13b/7b v1.5; wizardlm-30b/13b; codellama-34b/13b/7b instruct; openchat-13b v3.2; koala-13b; oasst-12b sft-4; dolly-12b v2; chatglm-6b v1.1; codegeex2-6b

inference.samples: one run per model per item; no repeated generations or multiple trials
inference.prompting: Thought + Action in one round (ReAct-style format), usually 1-shot CoT demonstration in task instruction; chat models get user/agent alternating turns; completion models get 'USER:'/'AGENT:' prefixes and a trailing 'AGENT:'

parameters.history_token_cap: 3500 tokens; minimum r chosen so (u0, ar, ur+1..uk) <=3500, then '[NOTICE] 2r messages are omitted.' appended to u0
parameters.token_estimate: word of length n = ceil(n/6) tokens; non-blank character = 1 token
parameters.round_limits: Avg rounds Table 2: OS 8, DB 5, KG 15, DCG 30, LTP 25, HH 35, WS 5, WB 10; OS default round limit 8; KG at most 15 actions

other.overall_score: per-task average across models rescaled to 1 (fixed reciprocal weights from Table 2 Weight-1: 10.8, 13.0, 13.9, 12.0, 3.5, 13.0, 30.7, 11.6; a ninth value 4.1 is printed), then averaged across tasks
other.toolkit: HTTP server-client, Docker per task, max-flow (Edmonds-Karp) scheduler

metrics.name: Success Rate (OS, DB, HH)
metrics.definition: fraction of items solved (OS exit code 0 for all checking scripts; DB exact match or table hash; HH goal reached)

metrics.name: Answer F1 (KG)
metrics.definition: F1 of predicted vs gold answer set

metrics.name: Reward (DCG)
metrics.definition: 0.7 x win rate + 0.3 x damage rate

metrics.name: Game Progress (LTP)
metrics.definition: proportion of ground-truth key points reached

metrics.name: Reward (WS)
metrics.definition: WebShop attribute/option/price match reward times r_type

metrics.name: Step Success Rate (WB)
metrics.definition: selected element correct and operation matches at the step

metrics.name: Overall Score (OA)
metrics.definition: weighted average of task scores using fixed reciprocal-mean weights

baselines: random and greedy strategies in Aquawar
no baseline for other tasks beyond other LLMs
eval.protocol: single run, greedy decoding, five outcome categories (Completed, CLE, IF, IA, TLE); LTP host and judge are gpt-3.5-turbo (human validation found auto eval more lenient on SGA/QR, esp. OSS models)

prompts.text: You are an assistant that will act like a person, I'will play the role of linux(ubuntu) operating system. Your goal is to implement the operations required by me or answer to the question proposed by me. For each of your turn, you should first think what you should do, and then take exact one of the three actions: "bash", "finish" or "answer".

I will ask you a question, then you should help me operate a MySQL database with SQL to answer the question. You have to explain the problem and your solution to me and write down your thoughts. ... Action: Operation ```sql SELECT * FROM table WHERE condition; ``` ... Action: Answer Final Answer: ["ANSWER1", "ANSWER2", ...]

prompts.purpose: KG tool-use instruction (7 tools, 1 demo, at most 15 actions)
prompts.text: You are an agent that answers questions based on the knowledge stored in a knowledge base. To achieve this, you can use the following tools to query the KB. ... You can take at most 15 actions to find the answer to the question.

This is a two-player battle game with four pet fish on each team. ... return your move with following JSON format: {'pick_fish': ..., 'action': 'choose from [normal, active]', 'target_position': "... you must choose from [0,3]"}
You are a game player, and you are playing Lateral Thinking Puzzle, also known as Situation Puzzle.
Interact with a household to solve a task. Imagine you are an intelligent agent in a household environment and your target is to perform actions to complete the task goal.
You are web shopping. I will give you instructions about what to do. You have to follow the instructions.

Based on the HTML webpage above, try to complete the following task: ... What should be the next action? Please select from the following choices (If the correct action is not in the page above, please select A. 'None of the above')

limits: Single run per model at temperature 0, no variance reported
Only simple CoT; ensembles, reflection and search not tested
OSS models limited to <=70B for compute reasons
LTP automatic host/judge is more lenient than humans; authors plan a dedicated host model
Dataset sizes are small (e.g. DCG 20 test items, LTP 50), and Table 2 test sizes differ from the appendix counts (KG 500 vs 150, WS 500 vs 200, WB 912 vs 100, HH 134 vs 50)
claude-3 and glm-4 scored after task weights fixed
Models are mid-2023 versions; since dated
